description: Rust oversized-result attempt after state and event staging
qualification: normal local combined-source Linux node with ephemeral demo trust and disposable JetStream
observations: The controlled Rust variant requested a 131073-byte canonical result after its state and event staging calls. The normal node returned HTTP 409 with a validated abort fence and no effect IDs.

A subsequent fresh query returned zero; namespace inspection showed zero state bytes and zero pending effects, and the real broker contained no messages. The node shut down cleanly and physically retired its state and effect owners; the fixture removed its own broker.

separateInstrumentedDiagnostic.observed: The separately rebuilt diagnostic node and component, using another disposable provider profile, observed an accepted state write and intent stage before a guest execution failure and fenced abort.

limitations: The normal-node abort does not itself identify the internal failure as the output-size validator; the separate instrumentation is diagnostic and uses another component and provider profile.
This does not establish all result boundaries, other guest languages, hosted CI, production trust or installed-distribution qualification. The node source includes unmerged work.
